Query Neo4j as the signed-in user

Source: R/backend__neo4j.R
oauth_db_neo4j_api.Rd

Run Cypher queries with each Shiny visitor's access token and Neo4j roles. The client uses the HTTPS Query API v2 and returns data frames, keeping nodes, relationships, paths and other nested values in list columns.

Usage

oauth_db_neo4j_api(
  authorization,
  url,
  database = "neo4j",
  target = NULL,
  required_scopes = character(),
  min_valid_for = 60,
  timeout = 30,
  ca_bundle = NULL,
  session = shiny::getDefaultReactiveDomain()
)

Arguments

authorization

Function providing the visitor's current sign-in authorization. Pass auth$connection from shinyOAuth without parentheses. To select a saved account, use a function calling auth$connection(id).

url

Neo4j HTTPS base URL, including any reverse-proxy prefix. Use the Query API host, not a neo4j+s:// or bolt:// connection URI.

database

Database name, default "neo4j".

target

Name of the service token to use in your shinyOAuth client. Named targets let one sign-in obtain tokens for different services. NULL uses the client's default token.

required_scopes

Additional OAuth permissions to check before use. Request them on the shinyOAuth client first; this check doesn't request consent or grant database privileges.

min_valid_for

Minimum remaining token lifetime, in seconds, when obtaining a token. Use 0 to accept any unexpired token.

timeout

Maximum seconds for one HTTP operation, including a read retry.

ca_bundle

Optional path to a trusted CA certificate bundle.

session

The visitor's Shiny session. Usually inferred when you create the helper inside server().

Value

A client object with these methods:

  • $query(statement, parameters = list(), raw = FALSE) runs one Cypher statement. Use named parameters such as list(name = "Alice") for $name placeholders. Returns a data frame, or the parsed Query API response with fields, values and metadata when raw = TRUE.

  • $execute(statement, parameters = list()) runs one statement and invisibly returns the server's update counters.

Details

Configure Neo4j Enterprise SSO to accept the provider's JWT access tokens and map users or groups to database roles. Aura requires a tier and SSO configuration that permit user-token access to the database's Query API. Console API credentials do not establish database access. Query API v2 requires Neo4j 5.19 or later; self-managed versions before 5.25 must enable it.

Create the client inside server(). Each call gets a current access token and discards responses after sign-out, account changes or lost required scopes. Requests require verified HTTPS, do not follow redirects and never replay a statement, including after HTTP 401. Neo4j query errors raise an error even when the server returns HTTP 202 or raw = TRUE.

Each statement uses an auto-commit transaction. There is no persistent Bolt connection, explicit transaction handle, automatic pagination or retained bookmark. A submitted write may commit after a client timeout; check its outcome before resubmitting it.

Parameters and results

Parameters are a named list of JSON-compatible values. Nested named lists become maps and unnamed lists become arrays. Missing scalar values become JSON null. Numbers must be finite; pass exact large integers as strings and convert them in Cypher with toInteger($value). Dates and timestamps become ISO strings; use date($value) or datetime($value) in the query.

Results use Neo4j's plain JSON format. Large JSON integers remain strings; temporal, spatial and binary values keep the server's string representation. Scalar columns of one type become atomic vectors; mixed or nested values remain lists. Empty or entirely null columns are logical. Duplicate field names are preserved. Use raw = TRUE for bookmarks, notifications and native graph values; discard saved results and metadata when changing users.

See also

vignette("neo4j", package = "shinyOAuthDB").

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
graph <- oauth_db_neo4j_api(auth$connection,
  url = "https://graph.example.org:7473", database = "neo4j")
output$rows <- shiny::renderTable({
  graph$query("MATCH (p:Person) WHERE p.country = $country RETURN p.name AS name LIMIT 20",
    parameters = list(country = "NL"))
})
} # }
